# Requirements

One plan, one height, one restart. An exported fork height and an exported plan name are the whole interface. At the block before the fork height every node schedules the plan for the fork height through the upgrade keeper, from its own begin blocker, with no governance proposal and no operator action; a chain whose module version map already carries the fork modules, which is every chain started from a full genesis, rejects the scheduling and is unaffected. At the fork height the node writes upgrade-info.json and stops, exactly as the SDK stops a node that lacks a handler, because the added stores must be mounted through the upgrade store loader before the block that initialises them runs; operators restart the same binary, the store loader mounts the six added stores with their initial version equal to the fork height, and the upgrade module's begin blocker applies the plan on the standard path: the handler runs the module migrations once, every module the version map lacks initialises from its own default genesis, and the done height is recorded. From that height the eight fork precompiles answer, and below it they do not, because the reachability predicate asks whether the activation plan has been applied at or before the height, or whether the chain's version map carried the modules from genesis, instead of asking whether any upgrade was ever applied.

## Requirement 1: One Plan That Brings The Fork Online At One Height

**User Story:** As the owner of a chain whose binary carries modules its state has never had, I want a single plan at a single height that mounts every missing store, initialises every missing module exactly once and turns the eight fork precompiles on together, so that the fork is a fact of the chain's history rather than a property of which binary a node happens to run.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature SHALL define one new upgrade plan with an exported name constant, registered with a handler of its own, and SHALL leave every plan name, handler and store-upgrade entry that already exists unchanged.
2. THE plan's store upgrades SHALL add exactly the module stores the pre-fork chain lacks - custody, anchor, exchange, bridge, launchpad and web search - SHALL add nothing else and SHALL delete and rename nothing, proven by a table test that derives the same set from the application's canonical store-key list and fails when a store is added to the application without being added to the plan.
3. THE plan's handler SHALL run the module migrations once against the version map read from state so that every module absent from that map initialises from its own default genesis exactly once, SHALL leave the web-search module paused with an empty attestor set, SHALL leave every other new module with its documented default parameters, and SHALL bring the module version map afterwards to the application's full version map.
4. THE plan's handler SHALL NOT register a remote asset, create a denomination or write a parameter no module's default genesis writes, and the registration of the fee token's remote asset SHALL be reported as a post-activation owner action through the bridge module's existing governance path because the chain record it needs is not defined in this repository as constants.
5. AN exported fork-height constant in the application package SHALL be the single place the activation height is written, and no configuration value, flag or governance parameter SHALL be able to change it for a built binary.
6. AT the height one below the fork height the application's begin blocker SHALL schedule the plan for the fork height through the upgrade keeper when no plan is scheduled and the plan has no done height, SHALL run after the module begin blockers so that no node panics for a binary updated before its trigger, and SHALL reject the scheduling on a chain whose module version map already carries every module the plan adds.
7. AT the fork height a node that did not start with the plan's upgrade-info.json SHALL write that file for the plan at that height and stop before the module begin blockers run, so that the block is not committed and the restarted binary mounts the plan's added stores through the upgrade store loader with their initial version equal to the fork height; a node that did start with that file SHALL proceed and let the upgrade module apply the plan on its standard path.
8. THE custom-precompile reachability predicate SHALL serve an address the activation record names only when the plan's done height is above zero and the block height is at or above it, or when the chain's module version map already carries every module the plan adds; it SHALL keep today's rule for every address the record does not name, and it SHALL NOT decide anything from the absence of every upgrade record.
9. ALL eight fork precompile addresses SHALL be named by the activation record, and tests SHALL prove that a state without the fork modules below the fork height serves none of the eight, that every legacy precompile is served in that same state, and that after the plan runs all eight are served.
10. TESTS SHALL prove that the begin blocker at one below the fork height schedules the plan on a chain whose version map lacks the fork modules and schedules nothing on a chain whose version map carries them, and no test in the repository SHALL be relaxed, skipped or deleted to make any of this pass.
